incidents.name: Monkswood Reservoir core leakage and downstream saturation
incidents.region: Cold Ashton / Monkswood Valley, South Gloucestershire (near Bath), England
incidents.location_label: Monkswood Reservoir, near Bath, United Kingdom
incidents.geo_source: British Place Names Monkswood Reservoir ST757711 51°26′18″N 2°21′1″W (reservoir centre)
incidents.river_or_facility: Monkswood Reservoir / SSSI valley north of Bath
incidents.cause_summary: EA: leakage through the upper puddle-clay core (top of core locally below overflow sill) saturated the downstream fill; 1931 subsidence.
incidents.what_happened: Monkswood is a 15.5 m puddle-clay-core embankment near Bath, completed 1895 (EA capacity 231×10³ m³; Wikipedia SSSI: reservoir built 1896, now Wessex Water). Founded on alluvium, peat and solifluction over Blue Lias; berms were added near the end of construction. EA 2011 incident 17: on 4 September 1931 a localised downstream-slope subsidence developed. Exploratory excavation found free-flowing water through the fill and internal erosion. Leakage on the downstream berm was significant only when the reservoir was within 0.3 m of top water; a gauging chamber showed flow rising sharply within 3 m of TWL. Trial pits later found the top of the core lower than the overflow sill in places. 1931–32 cement-sand grouting (about 280 t in 47 holes) cut leakage from 1.1 to 0.1 l/s, but by 1935 it had returned. 1945 sheet piles 6 m into the core had no effect. A 15 m single-phase slurry trench along the full crest in 1998 (Penman, Hoskins, Tedd & Harrison, BDS 2000) appears to have stopped the leak. No deaths.
incidents.status: Slurry-trench cut-off 1998; in service (Wessex Water).

incidents.name: Harlow Hill service reservoir downstream slip
incidents.region: Harlow Hill, Harrogate, North Yorkshire, England
incidents.location_label: Harlow Hill open service reservoir, Harrogate, United Kingdom
incidents.geo_source: Historic England Harlow Hill Water Tower SE2883854199 (Grade II, overlooks the Harrogate waterworks / service reservoir)
incidents.river_or_facility: Harlow Hill open service reservoir (Harrogate supply)
incidents.cause_summary: EA/Davies 1953: deep-seated downstream slip on 1:1.9 clay slopes after an extremely wet autumn; toe had been cut for a road and replaced by a retaining wall.
incidents.what_happened: Harlow Hill is a 9 m puddle-clay-core earthfill forming an open rectangular service reservoir perched about 70 m above Harrogate (EA: completed 1868, capacity 65×10³ m³; table built-year 1871). Embankments on three sides, slopes 1:1.9. EA 2011 incident 55: after an extremely wet autumn a major downstream slip on 18 December 1951 left a danger of breach. Vertical movement of 0.3 m on a slip plane beside the core, 0.23 m uplift at the toe against a concrete retaining wall, continuing at 0.01 m/h. Emergency day-and-night works: fastest possible drawdown; 33,000 sandbags and 400 t of sand in 'pavement buttresses' on the toe; tarpaulins; police ready to evacuate; well-points and attempted horizontal drains. History: upstream slips after construction and later; 1887 drought shrinkage cracks; a public road had removed about 3 m of toe. Fill was low-permeability clay; slopes always marginally stable. Davies (1953) published the case. No deaths.
incidents.status: Emergency toe weighting 1951; service reservoir still on Harlow Hill.

incidents.what_happened: Kype is a 17 m earth embankment built 1898 for Hamilton Town Council (EA capacity 670×10³ m³; Gazetteer for Scotland: 13.6 ha, 4 miles SE of Strathaven, now Scottish Water). The overflow is 35 m wide on natural ground. EA 2011 incident 79: after heavy rain in October 1977 the spillway-channel walls were overtopped at night and about 60 m³ of rock was eroded beside the channel, with minor damage at the mitre. A flood study and hydraulic model followed; the 1978 ICE Floods Guide design flow was three times the flood that overtopped the walls. 1982 works raised the upper spillway capacity, applied a proprietary mattress to one bank, and added a 650 mm precast wave wall on the crest (Little, 1984). No dam breach and no deaths.

incidents.cause_summary: EA/Musson: 6 m peat-and-earth mill dam with a narrow clay core, waterlogged after two days' rain, collapsed about eight hours after the 23 October 1839 Comrie ML 4.8 earthquake.
incidents.what_happened: The original Earlsburn dam was built for a consortium of mill owners southwest of Stirling, probably not long before 1839 (Pilot/history.scot: about four years old; 200-acre reservoir). EA 2011 incident 54: peat and earth with a narrow silty-clay core to rock, most of the dam on peat. A survey had pronounced it 'in a proper state of repair'. It collapsed some eight hours after the 23 October 1839 Comrie earthquake (ML 4.8, ~32 km away, PGA about 0.04 g — Hinks 2012 / Musson 1991). The flood caused several thousand pounds of damage; EA: no lives were lost. Musson concludes the earthquake triggered the burst even if it was not the principal cause — a poorly built 6 m bank waterlogged after two days of heavy rain. Falkirk Local History Society: later rebuilt by the Falkirk and Larbert Water Trust as a more substantial supply dam (today's Earlsburn No.1, Gazetteer, Scottish Water). Pin is the rebuilt reservoir on the same burn, not a surveyed 1839 crest.
incidents.status: Rebuilt as Earlsburn No.1 water-supply reservoir; in service (Scottish Water).

incidents.what_happened: Craig-y-Pistyll is a 13 m homogeneous embankment in Ceredigion, completed 1877 (EA capacity 350×10³ m³), founded on shale and built of weathered shaley matrix without a core or cut-off (a clay blanket was added in 1966). It supplies the Aberystwyth area (Dŵr Cymru; Wikipedia SSSI). EA 2011 incident 18: the reservoir was drawn down in 1939 for draw-off-tunnel repairs; the upstream face caved in. Lesson: long-term internal erosion had gone unobserved until drawdown. No deaths.

incidents.river_or_facility: Aldenham Reservoir / River Colne compensation (Grand Junction Canal)
incidents.cause_summary: EA: 1930s-Act recommendations led to stripping trees from crest and downstream shoulder; after January 1975 drawdown the uncompacted London Clay slipped upstream and downstream.
incidents.what_happened: Aldenham is a 7–9 m homogeneous London-Clay embankment completed 1795 (raised 1802) to compensate mill owners and the Grand Junction Canal (EA capacity 78×10³ m³; STRABAG/HCC: about 539,000 m³ and 480 m crest). EA 2011 incident 59: the bank had been prone to instability since construction. Early-1970s Reservoirs Act recommendations included removing all trees and undergrowth from the crest and upper downstream slope and a marginal crest raise. After drawdown in January 1975 two areas of the upstream slope slipped and two minor slips occurred on the 1:5 downstream slope. EA: vegetation had lowered pore pressures and rooted the surface; stripping it, possibly plus crest fill, was enough to allow movement. A shear surface was found at about 1 m depth. 1980s drainage trenches, 1990s sheet piling and later soil nailing did not fully stop movement (Heritage Gateway: trees removed 1975, gradual clay-fill movement). Hughes 2019 s.10 inspection: dam stable but needing longer-term repair. No deaths.
incidents.status: In service as a country-park reservoir; further embankment works reported 2020s.

incidents.name: Blackwater Dam thermal cracking (Kinlochleven)
incidents.region: Blackwater Reservoir above Kinlochleven, Highland, Scotland
incidents.location_label: Blackwater Dam, Kinlochleven, United Kingdom
incidents.geo_source: Historic Environment Scotland LB51833 NN 24765 60366
incidents.river_or_facility: Blackwater Reservoir / Kinlochleven hydro-aluminium scheme
incidents.cause_summary: EA: vertical cooling/hydration cracks shortly after completion of a mass-concrete gravity dam built without vertical construction joints.
incidents.what_happened: Blackwater is a 25 m mass-concrete gravity dam completed 1907 (EA; HES listing 1904–09) to power the Kinlochleven aluminium smelter (EA capacity 111,300×10³ m³). First UK dam with timber shuttering on both faces; granite displacers up to 10 t; no vertical construction joints, like contemporary Eigiau; narrow section; uplift not in the design. EA 2011 incident 93: shortly after completion, seven main vertical cracks up to 2.4 mm opened from the crest (barely perceptible at the base) and seeped. Worst cracking was in the northern part, attributed to faster summer-1908 placing and heat of hydration. Safety was not immediately threatened; silicate and fine grout failed to seal the cracks; peat drawn into the cracks reduced seepage. Later investigations (Morgan & Thomas 1961; Wallis et al. 2004) found the hearting generally sound. EA: the case helped introduce expansion joints on later British concrete dams. No deaths.
incidents.status: In service for hydro (smelter closed 2000; powerhouse still generates).

incidents.cause_summary: EA: first-filling storm waves exceeded the design height and displaced riprap on the 1:1.5 upstream face; prediction methods had underestimated wave height on a 4 km fetch.
incidents.what_happened: Megget is a 56 m gravel-fill embankment with a central asphaltic core, 570 m long, completed 1982 and opened 30 September 1983 (EA/Wikipedia capacity 61,400,000 m³) — the largest earth dam in Scotland, supplying Edinburgh. Maximum fetch 4 km along the prevailing wind. Upstream slope 1:1.5 with 1.8 m protection, the top 1.2 m heavy riprap to 900 mm. EA 2011 incident 85: during first filling a severe January 1984 storm damaged the riprap (Gallacher et al.); the same storm damaged Kielder blockwork. Further storms displaced individual stones or groups. No emergency action. Later pattern-grouting of riprap with bituminous grout (Hay-Smith 1998) increased mass while leaving ungrouted drainage panels. No deaths.
incidents.status: Pattern-grouted riprap; in service (Scottish Water).

incidents.what_happened: The unclassed Daze dam at Espeyrac (in service from the early 1970s; Wikipedia lake volume 150,000 m³; operator Ondulia later said maximum 48,000 m³) retains a head-pond on the ruisseau de la Daze above the Lot. ARIA 61508: about 01:30 on 6 December 2023 the reservoir emptied completely. A wave of 48,000 m³ (ARIA) ran 1.8 km down the Daze to the Lot. The operator had seen a small foundation leak 48 hours earlier and a larger hole about 15:00 the day before; it then grew until the pond drained. Cause: scour at the right-bank toe plus erosion under the dam. Six sheep drowned; a house's water and sewer connections and access track were damaged; two vehicles and farm kit were carried away. La Dépêche headline 150,000 m³ vs Ondulia/ARIA 30,000–48,000 m³ — ARIA/operator figures used for volume. No human deaths.
incidents.status: Cofferdam and foundation repairs ordered; site offline for months (Ondulia).

incidents.name: Ville-d'Avray / Étangs de Corot pond-dam water-main burst
incidents.location_label: Étangs de Corot / Ville-d'Avray pond dam, France
incidents.geo_source: Ministère des Sports / commune-mairie Étang de la Ville d'Avray 48.82010, 2.17940 (Rue des 2 Étangs)
incidents.river_or_facility: Étangs de Corot (Vieil Étang / Étang Neuf)
incidents.cause_summary: ARIA: a potable-water main through the pond embankment burst; water ran along the fill and through an existing downstream sinkhole.
incidents.what_happened: The Étangs de Corot at Ville-d'Avray are two 17th-century ponds (Vieil Étang and Étang Neuf) whose dikes feed the Saint-Cloud domain. ARIA 52504 (22 August 2018): about 13:45 a potable-water pipe crossing the pond dam burst. Water was present along about two-thirds of the embankment. Regulation gates were opened to hold the pond down; the leak was stopped about 16:00. Water had passed masonry-wall joints and an existing downstream-face sinkhole (fontis). Trenches were cut for repairs and backfilled; silt was cleared; the manager began moving utilities out of the dam. A 2016 hazard study had already classed the dikes C and warned of rupture risk to tens of thousands downstream (Val de Seine Vert / préfecture: about 30,000–33,000). Emergency consolidation works began autumn 2019 (CMN / franceinfo). No deaths.
incidents.status: Consolidation works from 2019 on both dikes (CMN).

incidents.cause_summary: ARIA / La Dépêche: a 4 m earth dike, unmaintained and riddled with animal burrows and brambles, breached over about 700 m in the January 2022 Garonne flood.
incidents.what_happened: ARIA 58547 (10 January 2022, Castelsarrasin): after severe flooding a 4 m earth dike ruptured and was heavily damaged over 700 m, flooding two residential quarters. Press (Radio Totem / La Dépêche / Journal Toulousain): the Bénis and Rivière Basse quarters, which had not flooded for decades, were inundated. The bank is one of about twenty ~century-old peasant dikes on the intercommunality, more than 3 km long; this reach had not been maintained, was overgrown with brambles, and was pierced by burrows, letting the Garonne in (Hugues Samain, Terres des Confluences). The communauté de communes plugged breaches in emergency with a mechanical excavator. No sourced death toll for this dike. Pin is the Bénis street/quarter, not a surveyed breach chainage.

incidents.name: La Faute-sur-Mer Digue Est (Xynthia overtopping)
incidents.location_label: Digue Est, La Faute-sur-Mer, Vendée, France

incidents.cause_summary: Nantes CAA / CETMEF: storm-surge overtopping of the named Digue Est along the Lay (about 2 hours); ASVL had not raised the dike. Cahiers Nantais: the Lay dike was overtopped without a breach; a separate dune breach occurred at La Belle-Henriette.
incidents.what_happened: On the night of 27–28 February 2010, storm Xynthia and a 102-coefficient tide overtopped the eastern protection dike of La Faute-sur-Mer along the Lay estuary (ouvrage « Digue Est », association syndicale de la Vallée du Lay). Nantes Cour administrative d'appel (2019): the submersion of Digue Est drowned several people in the commune and caused heavy damage; liability split commune 50%, State 35%, ASVL 15% (failure to raise the dike / PPRI / information). Wikigeotech/CETMEF: overtopping of the east dike lasted about 2 hours, water rising on average ~1 m/h (peaks 3–6 m/h); low spots were overtopped as far as the Braud barrage. Cahiers Nantais: the Lay dike was overtopped without rupturing; the sea also breached the ocean dune at La Belle-Henriette, creating a pincer. Ouest-France: water >1.5 m in the town. Deaths at La Faute-sur-Mer 29 (Norois / Chauveau; 12 further Xynthia deaths in Charente-Maritime are a different coast and are not copied here).
incidents.status: Post-Xynthia dike works and 'zone noire' clearances; commune merged 2022.

incidents.cause_summary: ARIA / DREAL: rapid irrigation drawdown after a dry summer produced a progressive 50 m upstream-face slide on the clay dike (about 25% of embankment length).
incidents.what_happened: ARIA 60110 (20 August 2022, Biarrotte, water-supply activity, EISH Orange): a crack was found on the upstream face of an irrigation-dam dike; three days later it widened into a slide involving a large volume of upstream fill, plan extent 50 m (25% of the embankment). The pond had been full two months earlier; in one month of heavier-than-usual irrigation half the storage was used, a drawdown rate never seen since construction. Control authority ordered the pool held at 14 m NGF / 200,000 m³, reinforced surveillance, a staff gauge, a detailed inspection and an approved safety diagnosis. Sud Ouest: Lac de Bédorède is a 22 ha / 600,000 m³ clay irrigation reservoir built 1993 south of Biarrotte for about 30 maize-seed farms; France Bleu: DREAL inspected the evolving upstream slide on 6 October and a December prefectural safety order required urgent earthworks. No source fetched reported deaths.
incidents.status: Pool held at ~200,000 m³ pending remédiation; public lakeside path closed for dike works.

A November inspection after partial drawdown found a ~60×40 cm hole under the structure on the canal side, dampness and cracks, and a damaged pond-drain plug, attributed to under-seepage (no cutoff), poor compaction and internal erosion. Château de Fontainebleau / OPPIC: the Henri IV Grand Canal (1606–08; 1.2 km; 140,000 m³; class C dikes) had east-end settlement from 2008 and leaks on the east and north return dikes over 190 m. A cofferdam was placed in the last third of the canal (~200 m upstream of the east dike) in September 2022 to dry masonry. On 14 December 2022 it slipped and failed under silt, forcing a method change. Waterproofing (east-dike injection, masonry, outfall) ran through 2023; the canal was rewatered April 2024 (€3.7 million recovery-plan works). No deaths.

incidents.what_happened: ARIA 59315 (1 July 2022, Suresnes, EISH Yellow): five remote operations in two days on the upper gate of pass no. 1 of a gated barrage, to damp upstream discharge swings, ended with rupture of the 'marteau' link between the right-bank brimbale and the upper gate. The operator saw abnormal over- and underflow, tried the lower gate (which sat askew), then cofferdammed the pass to keep the upstream pool above normal retention. Video and site inspection showed a 42 cm lack of level between banks and a jammed left-bank lifting-nut, so the offset mass broke the link and deformed the counter-guide. Next day both gates were lifted clear and re-levelled. Pass 2 and the flap weir still worked; emergency cofferdams used as a spare gate on pass 1 were no longer available if pass 2 failed. French Wikipedia: the Suresnes barrage-écluse (quai Gallieni; three locks, two barrages split by Île de Puteaux) is the automated Seine navigation weir. No deaths.
incidents.status: Gates re-levelled; spare cofferdam function on pass 1 unavailable pending repairs.

incidents.name: Presa de Buseo (DANA 2024 overtopping)
incidents.location_label: Presa de Buseo, Chera, Valencia, Spain
incidents.geo_source: Spanish Wikipedia Embalse de Buseo 39°35′37″N 0°56′36″W
incidents.river_or_facility: Presa de Buseo / Río Reatillo (Turia)
incidents.cause_summary: Generalitat report to the DANA judge: with the bottom outlet and two of three intakes out of service, the 1915 gravity dam overtopped the crest by about 2 m and the parapet broke.
incidents.what_happened: On 29 October 2024 the DANA filled Presa de Buseo (Chera; built 1903–15; 40 m gravity; 7.05–7.5 hm³). El Diario / Las Provincias citing the Consell report to the investigating judge: only irrigation intake no. 3 (rehabilitated 2020, ~9.2 m³/s) was usable; the century-old bottom outlet and intakes 1–2 were out of service, and intake 3 sat above most of the rising pool until 18:05. The reservoir reached spillway level 458.70 m about 21:45–21:50 (7.2 hm³), then overtopped the 460.40 m crest about 22:10 (8.54 hm³) and rose to the parapet, spilling at the abutments. Peak volume 8.88 hm³ (125% of 7.05). FNCA/MITECO diagnosis: complete overtopping and signs of disintegration, a direct rupture threat to Sot de Chera. The dam did not collapse. No source fetched gave deaths at this dam (Valencia DANA regional totals are not copied).
incidents.status: Overtopped; parapet damaged; dam standing. Auxiliary outlets were inoperable on the day.

incidents.name: Presa de Forata (DANA 2024 spillway damage)
incidents.location_label: Presa de Forata, Yátova, Valencia, Spain
incidents.geo_source: Spanish Wikipedia Embalse de Forata 39°20′41″N 0°52′01″W

incidents.cause_summary: MITECO/CHJ: an inflow above the 10,000-year design passed the gated spillway (peak out ~1,092 m³/s); emergency works later rebuilt a scoured stilling-basin counter-weir and left-bank scour — the dam did not overtop or collapse.
incidents.what_happened: MITECO integrated report on Forata in DANA 2024: inflow peak >2,016 m³/s (SAIH), above the dam-safety 10,000-year figure; outflow peak 1,092 m³/s (about 1,000-year). The reservoir rose from 5.4 hm³ at 08:30 to 39.3 hm³ at 20:30 on 29 October; spillway flow began 17:30 at the weir crest; maximum level 384.9 m at 21:10, 4.2 m below the 389.1 m crest. About 74.59 hm³ was spilled 29 Oct 17:30–1 Nov 00:00. The dam did not fail. CHJ emergency-works fiche: reconstruct ~30 m of stilling-basin counter-weir (~3 m high), concrete a 3 m left-bank scour, replace basin fill, restore the intake and a silted bottom outlet, and close a right-bank low spot that could spill beside the crest. Wikipedia: the 1970 CHJ gravity dam (68 m; 37 hm³) started the day at 14.16% full and cut Magro peak. No source fetched gave deaths at this dam (Valencia DANA regional totals are not copied).
incidents.status: Dam standing; emergency stilling-basin and access repairs (CHJ).

incidents.name: Les Boucholeurs sea walls and dunes (Xynthia)

incidents.cause_summary: Paralia / CMC 2015–2016 Xynthia case study: northern sea walls failed to stop wave overtopping (wave breaking caused two deaths); southern dunes were fragile and marsh storage was exceeded.
incidents.what_happened: On 27–28 February 2010, storm Xynthia flooded Les Boucholeurs, the oyster-farming village astride Châtelaillon-Plage and Yves. France Digues: water reached 1.60 m in the rear of the village; about 400 people were housed that night. Paralia (Coastal flood protection systems, Xynthia feedback): to the north, sea walls did not protect enough against overtopping and wave breaking caused two deaths; to the south, dunes were very fragile and swamp storage was exceeded; the Port Punay canal directed flow into the low urban cell. Thirty-eight houses were later bought out (association Les Boucholeurs). Ministry of Ecology / E3S name the Boucholeurs district protection among post-Xynthia Charente-Maritime works. Do not copy 47 national Xynthia deaths onto this site.
incidents.status: New sea wall and breakwaters built (Xynthia +20 cm); 38 houses demolished.
incidents.affected_or_evacuated: About 400 people housed overnight (France Digues)

incidents.what_happened: Le Bien Public: on Sunday 29 May 2016 around noon the dike of Étang de Cassin failed; four other dikes including Étang de Matrot, immediately downstream on the Argentalet at La Roche-en-Brenil, then suffered the same fate. incidents.what_happened: On 5 July 2017 at about 07:00 the municipal water-supply pond above Valverde de la Vera (Cáceres) burst. Hoy and Digital Extremadura: water and mud ran through streets, damaged houses, the municipal pool and EX-203. Consejero Navarro: the pond held about 60,000 of 100,000 m³ and emptied. TSJ Extremadura (Feb 2022) held the Junta liable (€127,647.98 to Generali): piping at the intake-tower waterproofing, reception 29 Aug 2016, pond full for months. The Ayuntamiento had repeatedly asked for leak repairs and was not held responsible.
incidents.status: Pond emptied 2017; Junta held civilly responsible 2022. Emergency works followed.

incidents.what_happened: In the night of 16–17 March 2025 the 1994 Junta irrigation pond La Maricana above Jarandilla de la Vera failed. 112 Extremadura / Guardia Civil: about 05:15 on Monday 17 March a mass of water entered the town, swept cars and cut EX-119 at km 31; two people evacuated; no personal injuries. Hoy: about 310,000 m³ released; 360 ha of tobacco and paprika left without irrigation. Built 1994 over the buried Arroyo de la Maricana; patched 2012; CHT inspected 2022. CHT later said the pond was built without its authorisation, had no approved emergency plan after 2022, and may not be rebuilt on the stream. Juntaex (31 Jul 2025): reconstruction prohibited by CHT; a replacement pond is being planned.
incidents.status: Failed 17 Mar 2025. CHT forbids rebuild on the buried stream. Replacement pond planned.

incidents.what_happened: Europa Press (6 May 2011 technical briefing) and Contigo La Palma: the first rupture of Laguna de Barlovento's synthetic liner was in 2005, when water reached about 24 m above the lowest point. Drains between liner and ground ran at a barely controllable rate. After emptying, a generalised settlement had broken the perimeter drain and the liner, with a central hole about 50 m across and up to 3 m deep toward the bottom outlet. A 2006 repair (~€3 million) filled the hole and added a new drain gallery but left the perimeter drain unfixed. The 16 April 2011 tears are a later incident (barlovento-2011-04-16). No source fetched gave deaths in 2005.
incidents.status: Repaired 2006; failed again 2011.

incidents.name: Mondego right-bank dike at Casais / A1 km 191 (2026)
incidents.region: Casais / São Martinho do Bispo, Coimbra
incidents.location_label: Dique dos Casais at A1 viaduto C do Mondego, Coimbra, Portugal
incidents.geo_source: Nominatim Casais halt, São Martinho do Bispo 40.2047717, -8.4838798. Lusa/Proteção Civil: right-bank breach at Casais beside the A1 bridge, km 191.
incidents.river_or_facility: Dique da margem direita do canal principal do Mondego (Ponte dos Casais / viaduto C)
incidents.cause_summary: Lusa/ANEPC: right-bank main-channel dike at Casais under the A1 overtopped and breached about 17:45 on 11 Feb 2026 at >2,100 m³/s. UC working group later cited protection works not functioning, A1-pier debris and vegetation-weakened slopes.
incidents.what_happened: Lusa via TSF/CNN Portugal/Expresso: at about 17:45 on 11 February 2026 the right-bank main-channel dike of the Mondego at Casais, Coimbra, breached beside the A1 viaduct (Proteção Civil: km 191). Flow about 2,100 m³/s (RTP). Water flooded the São Martinho do Bispo irrigation block toward Montemor-o-Velho. ANEPC commander Mário Silvestre: at that stage no significant village impacts, water going into fields. Brisa closed A1 km 189–198; about 23:00 the north abutment fill of Viaduto C collapsed at km 191.2 after the dike had excavated it (government/Brisa). A1 reopened after about 15 days. University of Coimbra later listed failed protection works, A1-pier log jams and vegetation. No source fetched gave deaths at this dike. February 2026 storm/national flood deaths are not copied. Distinct from mondego-casais-2001-01-27.
incidents.status: Breached 11 Feb 2026; A1 abutment rebuilt and reopened. UC report on causes published later.

incidents.location_label: Mondego dike at Formoselha, Montemor-o-Velho, Portugal
incidents.geo_source: Nominatim hamlet Formoselha, Santo Varão 40.1788600, -8.6156045. Câmara/Lusa: dike 'junto a Formoselha' burst Saturday 21 Dec 2019.
incidents.river_or_facility: Dique do canal principal do Mondego at Formoselha
incidents.cause_summary: Câmara de Montemor-o-Velho / Lusa: main-channel Mondego dike beside Formoselha burst about 16:30–16:35 on 21 Dec 2019, sending 400–500 m³/s into the vale central.
incidents.what_happened: JN/PT Jornal/Lusa: about 16:30 on Saturday 21 December 2019 the Câmara de Montemor-o-Velho declared maximum flood alert after the Mondego main-channel dike 'junto a Formoselha' burst. Low areas of Carapinheira, Montemor-o-Velho, Meãs do Campo, Tentúgal and Ereira were warned. PT Jornal later: 400–500 m³/s from the Formoselha hole into the vale central, loading the right peripheral dike. RTP: local junta president João Girão said municipal roads were under water and some houses had about 3 m of water. More than 250 people had already been taken from homes in Montemor-o-Velho. No source fetched gave deaths at this dike. Distinct from the 22 Dec Casal Novo peripheral-dike collapse and from 2001/2026 Casais.
incidents.status: Breached 21 Dec 2019; vale central flooded.

incidents.what_happened: Público (22 Dec 2019) and ECO/Renascença: after afternoon evacuation of Casal Novo do Rio for an imminent peripheral-dike failure, mayor Emílio Torrão confirmed about 22:00 a second Mondego dike rupture on the left bank of the right peripheral channel, opposite Casal Novo do Rio, about 1.5 km away.
